title: 世界宗教 Day 18：巴哈伊信仰
title_en: World Religions Day 18: The Bahá'í Faith

questions.question: 巴哈伊信仰的「渐进启示」如何看待摩西、佛陀、耶稣、穆罕默德与巴哈欧拉之间的关系？
options: 同一序列上的显示者：灵性教诲不变，社会律法随时代更新，巴哈欧拉也不是最后一位
巴哈欧拉是众先知的封印，前面各位的启示都是在为他铺路，此后不会再有新的显示者出现
各宗教教义本质上完全等价，所以信徒可以同时保留原来的宗教身份、混合信奉多种宗教
显示者都是神的道成肉身，因而每一位所说的律法都永久有效、不会更新
questions.explanation: 渐进启示把各位显示者看成同一位教师面向不同时代的连续课程：灵性教诲不变，律法制度因时而设，巴哈欧拉之后至少一千年还会有下一位。「封印」恰是伊斯兰主流对穆罕默德的定位，也是它不接受巴哈伊的原因；「各教等价可混信」是常见误解。
questions.question_en: How does the Bahá'í doctrine of progressive revelation see the relationship between Moses, the Buddha, Jesus, Muhammad and Bahá'u'lláh?
options_en: They are Manifestations in one series: the spiritual teachings stay constant, the social laws are renewed for each age, and Bahá'u'lláh is not the last
Bahá'u'lláh is the seal of the prophets; the earlier revelations prepared for him and no Manifestation will come after
All religions are doctrinally equivalent, so believers may keep their old religious identity and practise a blend
Each Manifestation is God incarnate, so every law any of them gave remains binding forever
questions.explanation_en: Progressive revelation treats the Manifestations as successive lessons from one teacher to different ages: spiritual teachings persist, laws and institutions change, and another Manifestation is expected no sooner than a thousand years after Bahá'u'lláh. The 'seal of the prophets' is mainstream Islam's claim about Muhammad and the very reason it rejects the Bahá'í Faith; 'all religions are the same, mix freely' is a common misreading.

questions.question: 印度巴哈伊机构报出约 200 万信徒，人口普查却只有几千人自报为巴哈伊。最合理的解释是什么？
options: 两把尺子不同：一个数名册上签过入教声明的人，一个数普查时自报这个宗教的人
大批信徒受到迫害后不敢在人口普查中表明身份，所以普查结果严重低估了真实人数
教会机构为了扩大影响而系统性地夸大人数，普查数字才是真实规模
大多数人入教后不久又集体退出，名册没有及时更新，两边统计年份也不同
questions.explanation: 落差不是谁在说谎，而是名册登记与自我申报两种口径的差别；普查员按姓名归类宗教、入教又不改名，进一步拉大差距。因受迫害而隐瞒身份更像伊朗的情形，原文对印度的解释是统计口径。
questions.question_en: Bahá'í institutions in India report about two million members, while the national census counts only a few thousand self-identified Bahá'ís. What best explains the gap?
options_en: The two figures use different yardsticks: one counts people who signed a declaration and remain on the rolls, the other counts people who name the religion themselves at the census
Many believers hide their identity in the census for fear of persecution, so the census badly undercounts
The institutions systematically inflate their numbers for influence, and the census shows the true size
Most converts soon left en masse, the rolls were never updated, and the two counts come from different years
questions.explanation_en: The gap is not a matter of anyone lying but of registration versus self-report; census takers in rural India often assign religion by name, and converts do not change their names. Hiding for fear of persecution fits Iran better; for India the explanation is the counting method.

questions.question: 巴哈伊与新教都反对教阶制，结果一个几乎没有分支，一个分出无数教派。关键区别在哪里？
options: 巴哈伊保留了一个世袭的神职阶层来裁定教义，新教彻底取消了任何形式的神职
巴哈伊把权威交给写定的继承文本和选举出的九人合议，新教则推向个人良心与经文
巴哈伊历史短、人口少，还没来得及分裂；新教只是因为传播时间更长、地域更广才分出了教派
巴哈伊允许每位信徒自行定义教义，分歧都在私人层面消化，不会公开分裂
questions.explanation: 巴哈伊废除神职后，把解释权写进「圣约」的继承链，事务交给无提名、无竞选选出的九人合议，另立权威者被判为违约者；代价是解释弹性小、个人缺少制度化异议渠道。它没有任何神职阶层，也不允许个人把自己的理解当作权威教义推行。
questions.question_en: Both the Bahá'í Faith and Protestantism rejected clerical hierarchy, yet one has almost no sects and the other has countless. What is the key difference?
options_en: The Bahá'í Faith kept a hereditary priesthood to rule on doctrine, while Protestantism abolished every form of clergy
The Bahá'í Faith vests authority in a written line of succession and elected nine-member councils, while Protestantism pushed authority to individual conscience and scripture
The Bahá'í Faith is younger and smaller and simply hasn't had time to split; Protestantism just spread for longer
The Bahá'í Faith lets each believer define doctrine personally, so disagreements stay private and never become public splits
questions.explanation_en: Having abolished clergy, the Bahá'í Faith wrote interpretive authority into the Covenant's line of succession and handed affairs to nine-member bodies elected without nominations or campaigning; anyone setting up a rival authority is declared a Covenant-breaker. The cost is less interpretive flexibility and no institutional channel for dissent. There is no clergy at all, and individuals may not promote their own understanding as authoritative.
